messages.content: 你能先找出法國在1800年至1900年間與「戰爭」和「經濟」有關的重要歷史事件嗎？之後，你可以告訴我藝術家「奧古斯特·羅丹」創作的雕塑「沉思者」的現在市場價值嗎？最後，我也想知道1882年創作的雕塑「吻」的市場價值，也是由「奧古斯特·羅丹」創作的。

function.name: get_sculpture_value
function.description: Retrieve the current market value of a particular sculpture by a specific artist. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist who created the sculpture.

year.description: The year the sculpture was created. This is optional and is not required for all sculptures. Default is the current year.

function.name: history_get_key_events
function.description: Retrieve key historical events within a specific period for a certain country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

country.description: The name of the country for which history is queried.

start_year.description: Start year of the period for which history is queried.

end_year.description: End year of the period for which history is queried.

event_type.description: Types of event. If none is provided, default that all types will be considered.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1) Key historical events in France between 1800-1900 related to War and Economy.

We need to call history_get_key_events with country="France", start_year=1800, end_year=1900, event_type=["War","Economy"] (or maybe separate calls? But we can pass array). According to tool signature, event_type param type is union of strings or array? It says `event_type?: "War" | "Revolutions" | "Diplomacy" | "Economy"[].` That seems like an array of those options. So we should provide ["War","Economy"]. Good.

Then ask about Auguste Rodin's sculpture "Thinker". Actually it's called "Le Penseur" but okay. We want its current market value. Use get_sculpture_value with sculpture="Thinking Man"? Wait actual title "The Thinker" but they wrote "沉思者" Chinese translation. Provide sculpture="The Thinker" or "沉思者"? Might use English. We'll give both? Let's just use "The Thinker".

Also second request: sculpture "Kissing" from 1882 by Rodin. That's "L'Embrasseuse"? Actually "The Kiss" is "Le Baiser" by Rodin, made around 1887-88. They say 1882; maybe referencing "La Valse"? Not sure. Anyway we'll query with sculpture="The Kiss" year=1882.

But note: For first sculpture no year needed. For second include year=1882.

We'll make two calls to get_sculpture_value accordingly.

Thus produce three function calls sequentially. Probably best to do them one after another. In JSON format each call separately. Then output results.
